Why this is better

One scale, one selected state

The connected geometry removes visual debris. A single dark selected segment gives authority without resembling stars, ratings, or a spreadsheet grid.

Use blocks only when count itself has meaning.
Use a segmented rail when the user is choosing one state from an ordered scale.

06 · Implementation handoff

Production specification

Build polished analytical controls for a case-management platform. THREE-POINT RANGE - Use React Aria multi-thumb slider behavior. - Render one continuous rail. - Low and high use circular boundary handles. - Expected uses a diamond or vertical-rule marker. - Fill the interval between low and high. - Print Low, Expected, and High values explicitly. - Constrain low <= expected <= high. - Support touch, keyboard arrows, Home/End, and visible focus. - State uncertainty redundantly in text. DISCRETE JUDGMENT - Use one connected segmented control with six ordered states. - Avoid isolated squares, stars, free sliders, and numeric text fields. - Display a qualitative label for the selected state. - Preserve author and timestamp metadata separately. ANALYTICAL DISPLAYS - Prefer intervals, rules, points, and directly labeled bars. - Use Observable Plot for uncertainty and evidence-rich displays. - Use Recharts for bespoke responsive product charts. - Use Tremor only as implementation material, not as the visual identity. - Avoid anonymous bars, card soup, decorative donuts, and charts without decision meaning.
